ASTRA ASSEMBLY INVESTIGATION — SECOND-STAGE CONSTRUCTION
2026-11-01

DECISION

The consequential opening survives, but the preferred mechanism has changed.
Temporary guides are no longer the main route. I constructed a completion-
dependent physical recovery operation, exposed and removed an avoidable
recycling bypass, then allowed a stronger conventional recovery process to
take over most of that service. Its possible integration advantage is too
narrow and unmeasured to carry the ambition.

The principal target is now manufacture of a continuous, chemically specified
23S RNA without taking that RNA from an existing ribosome, followed by
repeatable full translation. The independent covalent construction supplied
an exact material route. I reconciled it with the functional recovery work,
complete cost accounting and a matched preparation experiment that separates
chemical specification, material damage and inherited folding history.

There is no new wet-lab result, demonstrated resource advantage, closed
factory or proven general assembly principle here. The return consists of
specific molecular constructions, actual structural/chemical source analysis,
ordinary proofs, executable evidence, and failures that changed the choice.

WHY THIS CAPABILITY MATTERS

A manufactured ribosome is a potentially general machine for making other
protein machines. Existing purified-component constructions still leave
important dependencies on native RNA, undefined extracts, supplied factors,
modified precursors or living-system production. Removing the native-RNA
dependence would enable deliberate chemical construction of the machine's
central scaffold, including chemical states that a DNA sequence alone does
not specify. That is a substantial molecular-manufacturing capability even
before autonomous reproduction is possible.

The target is a material object with known chemical composition and measured
working service. Recovering its rRNA genotype through reverse transcription
and PCR is a different service; those operations do not reproduce its full
modification pattern or assembled state. Normal recycling can re-pair
subunits, so the retained identity is a23S/50S lineage, not a permanent70S pair.

CHEMICAL ASSEMBLY AND COMPLETION-DEPENDENT RECOVERY
Research record, 2026-11-01

STATUS
This is a source-constrained molecular construction and an experimental
decision, not a new wet-lab result. No assembly yield, kinetic discrimination,
fidelity or lifetime is inferred from a contact graph or assigned to the new
construct. Existing catalytic selection, ribosome display, covalent RNA
ligation and natural remodeling are credited as existing machinery.

THE SERVICE
Manufacture a continuous, chemically specified 23S RNA without extracting
that RNA from a preexisting ribosome; assemble it with explicit structural
proteins; recover the same manufactured 50S/23S lineage after a complete
translation challenge; and obtain repeated, accurate protein output over a
declared working interval. Small subunits, tRNAs, translation factors, energy
regeneration and processing enzymes remain explicit supplied components.

The long-term consequence would be a chemically programmable route to
large RNA-protein machines, with the ribosome as an unusually consequential
first target. It would remove a native-RNA/extract dependence in the productive
path. It would not by itself produce a self-replicating factory, manufacture
modified monomers, or eliminate biological production of supplied enzymes.

The independent chemical construction is now the main manufacturing lead.
The root completion-exit construction is a candidate qualification/harvesting
operation within it. The informed conventional competitor already provides
most of the same recovery service. I do not make uniqueness or total-cost

# Separately deprotect the PTC patches, then restore the native backbone

## Decision

The strongest refinement is to replace the proposed 80-nt patch at positions 2437–2516 with a **52-nt D/Ψ patch and a 28-nt dense mixed patch**, join them covalently, and retain the ordinary magnesium/temperature reconstitution baseline. This localizes the critical chemistry experiment and avoids exposing D to the ho5C synthesis/deprotection workflow. It does **not** establish that the dense four-modification patch has already been made.

I do not presently claim that a ligation splint can select the productive ribosome assembly path. An aligned, ligatable nick is a local chemical condition. A misfolded RNA can satisfy that condition, and a globally productive fold can hide its nick. Removing the splint also removes its imposed geometry. Neither the DALI results nor the modified-nucleotide extension results demonstrate global fold discrimination, reusable resetting of a chemically intact 23S ribosome, full translation fidelity, or working lifetime.

## Exact practical refinement

Positions refer to the 2,904-nt ENA V00331.1 reference already checked against 4YBB entity 22. G2445 remains unmodified during chemical manufacture and is later methylated by RlmKL.

| Patch | Positions | Length | Marks |
|---|---|---:|---|
| DP52 | 2437–2488 | 52 nt | D2449, Ψ2457 |
| DENSE28 | 2489–2516 | 28 nt | Cm2498, ho5C2501, m2A2503, Ψ2504 |

The modification-annotated sequences are:

```text
DP52
GUACUCCGGGGA[D]AACAGGC[Psi]GAUACCGCCCAAGAGUUCAUAUCGACGGCGG

DENSE28
UGUUUGGCA[Cm]CU[ho5C]G[m2A][Psi]GUCGGCUCAUCA
```

The new bond is after G2488, before U2489. Both nick termini are canonical ribonucleotides with the usual 3′-OH/5′-phosphate chemistry. Cm2498 is inside the right 12-nt splint flank, so the original calculation for modification-free local duplexes cannot be copied to this junction. Full-length product purification and chemical qualification remain necessary.

Gasparutto et al. chemically synthesized a natural *E. coli* alanine tRNA containing D, ribothymidine and Ψ and measured alanine acceptance.
